about: A storage system that spreads files across many servers and lets apps reach them in several ways.

prs.title: Copies say which version they came from
prs.broken: Copying a file from a bucket that keeps old versions never said which version was copied.
prs.changed: Copies now report the source version, as Amazon S3 does.
prs.matters: Backup and sync tools can tell exactly what they copied.

prs.title: Bucket permissions can be set when sign-in is off
prs.broken: With no users set up, every request to set a bucket's access rule failed, even the plain private one.
prs.changed: The server now accepts these rules when sign-in is turned off.
prs.matters: People running SeaweedFS without accounts can set bucket access like on AWS.

prs.title: SFTP no longer creates missing folders on its own
prs.broken: Making a folder or uploading a file inside a folder that did not exist quietly created every missing folder on the way. A normal SFTP server says the folder does not exist.
prs.changed: The SFTP server now refuses both with a clear not-found error when the parent folder is missing, the same answer OpenSSH gives.
prs.matters: Scripts that move files over SFTP catch a wrong path right away instead of filling storage with stray folders.

prs.title: Storage servers no longer say an old copy is current
prs.broken: When an app asked a storage server if its copy of a file was still current, the server checked the date first and could say yes even when the fingerprint did not match.
prs.changed: The server now checks the fingerprint first and looks at the date only when no fingerprint is sent, as the web standard says. Lists, "any" and loose fingerprints now match too.
prs.matters: Apps and caches do not keep a stale copy of a file, and they skip downloads they do not need.

prs.title: File checks now understand lists of fingerprints
prs.broken: Apps can ask for a file only if it matches, or does not match, a fingerprint they already have. SeaweedFS compared the whole request as one value, so the "any" marker, a list of fingerprints and loose fingerprints never matched.
prs.changed: These checks now handle "any", lists and loose fingerprints, using the strict or loose comparison each check calls for in the web standard.
prs.matters: Browsers and caches that send these checks stop downloading the full file again when they already have it.

prs.title: Asking for part of a file's details now gets the right answer
prs.broken: Apps can ask for just the details of a file, limited to a slice of it. SeaweedFS ignored the slice and described the whole file, and a slice past the end still got an OK.
prs.changed: Those requests now report the size of the slice asked for, the same way a download of that slice does, and a slice past the end gets the error Amazon S3 gives.
prs.matters: Apps built for S3 that check a range before downloading get the same answers they would from Amazon.

prs.title: Conditional uploads now say "not found" for a missing file
prs.broken: An app can upload a file only if the server's copy still matches what it read. When the file was missing, SeaweedFS said "precondition failed" instead of "not found" like Amazon S3, so apps could not tell missing from changed.
prs.changed: Uploads, copies and multipart uploads with that check now answer "not found" when there is no current file. A changed file still gets "precondition failed".
prs.matters: Apps built for S3 react correctly when the file they expect is gone.

prs.title: File transfer listings no longer hang or come back short
prs.broken: SeaweedFS can serve files over SFTP, a common way to transfer files. If storage hiccupped during a folder listing, the server got stuck forever, and a single hidden file could cut a big listing short.
prs.changed: I made a storage error end the listing with a clear failure, and made hidden files stop cutting the listing short.
prs.matters: Users see every file they are allowed to see, or a clear error, never a silently partial list or a stuck server.

prs.title: Resumed file uploads no longer wipe the start of the file
prs.broken: When an upload over SFTP was cut off and then resumed, the server kept the new part but replaced everything before it with zeros. The file looked complete but was damaged, with no error.
prs.changed: When a file is opened to continue writing, the server now starts from the bytes already there instead of an empty copy.
prs.matters: Resuming a big upload gives back the whole file, not a silently broken one.

prs.title: Small files read over WebDAV are no longer blank
prs.broken: SeaweedFS keeps very small files inside its index instead of in separate pieces. Reading one over WebDAV, a way to open server files like a network drive, gave the right size but all zeros.
prs.changed: I made WebDAV read those small files from where they are kept.
prs.matters: Settings files and other small files open with their real content, and copying them no longer makes blank copies.

prs.title: Small files uploaded by form keep their size
prs.broken: A file uploaded by form and stored inside its own record kept its bytes but was recorded as 0 bytes. Downloads, listings and WebDAV then treated it as empty.
prs.changed: That upload now records the real size and checksum, the same as other uploads.
prs.matters: Small config files uploaded this way can be read back.

prs.title: New folders over WebDAV show up every time
prs.broken: Creating a folder over WebDAV with a name that had been used before said it worked but made nothing. File managers lost the second "New Folder" after a rename, and a deleted folder could not be made again.
prs.changed: I fixed how the folder name was split from its path, so the folder itself is created and not an empty name inside it.
prs.matters: Folders made from a file manager on a WebDAV share appear as expected.

prs.title: Deleting a folder over WebDAV deletes what is inside
prs.broken: Over WebDAV, a folder with anything in it could not be deleted, and nothing could be moved or copied on top of an existing folder.
prs.changed: I made deletes remove the folder with its contents, with checks so a move or upload can never wipe the wrong folder.
prs.matters: File managers that mount SeaweedFS can clean up and reorganize folders normally.

prs.title: Folder entries that hold data now list their real size
prs.broken: In SeaweedFS's S3 storage, a name ending in a slash can hold data. Reading it gave back the data, but a folder listing said its size was zero.
prs.changed: The listing now counts the data stored with such an entry, and empty ones still show zero.
prs.matters: Apps that trust listing sizes see the same size they get when they read the file.

prs.title: Listing unfinished uploads now follows the S3 rules
prs.broken: The list of unfinished uploads ignored where to resume, came back in the wrong order, and could claim there was more when the page was complete.
prs.changed: The list is now sorted by name, resumes after the given name, and reports whether there is more and where to continue.
prs.matters: Tools that page through uploads end cleanly and miss nothing.

prs.title: A deleted user policy stays deleted
prs.broken: In the built-in IAM API, asking for a user policy that did not exist, or had just been deleted, still returned a policy made up from the user's permissions.
prs.changed: If the user has stored policies and none has that name, it now answers that the policy does not exist, like the standalone IAM server does.
prs.matters: Tools that check whether a policy was removed get the right answer.

prs.title: Resumed downloads start over when the file has changed
prs.broken: A client resuming a download asks for the rest of the file only if it has not changed. The filer and volume server ignored that check and sent bytes from the new version.
prs.changed: Both servers now send the whole current file when the version check fails, and the requested part only when it still matches.
prs.matters: Resumed downloads no longer glue pieces of two different versions into one corrupt file.

prs.title: Reading a deleted file in a versioned bucket answers like S3
prs.broken: On a versioned bucket, reading a key whose latest version is a delete marker gave a plain not found, with no sign that it had been deleted.
prs.changed: The reply now says it is a delete marker and gives its version, and asking for the marker itself returns method not allowed, as S3 does.
prs.matters: Backup and sync tools can tell a deleted file from one that never existed.

prs.title: WebDAV copy onto a folder no longer deletes the folder
prs.broken: Copying a file onto a folder's address over WebDAV, with overwrite on, failed with an error, and the folder and everything in it were gone afterwards.
prs.changed: The copy now replaces the folder with the file as asked, and with overwrite off the folder stays untouched.
prs.matters: A WebDAV client can no longer wipe out a folder of files with a copy that then fails.

prs.title: S3 lists of unfinished uploads now group by folder
prs.broken: When listing unfinished multipart uploads with a folder separator, SeaweedFS ignored the separator and returned every upload in the bucket at the top level.
prs.changed: Uploads below a folder are now grouped under that folder's prefix, the way Amazon S3 does it.
prs.matters: Tools that browse pending uploads folder by folder see the right ones instead of the whole bucket.

prs.title: Listing buckets works when login is turned off
prs.broken: With login turned off, SeaweedFS let anyone create and use storage buckets, but the list of buckets always came back empty.
prs.changed: With login off, the list now shows every bucket, as it did in older versions.
prs.matters: Tools that list buckets before using them work again on servers without login.

prs.title: Bucket ownership settings work when login is turned off
prs.broken: With login turned off, anyone could create and write to a bucket, but reading or changing its ownership settings was always refused.
prs.changed: With login off, these ownership requests are now allowed, like the other bucket requests already were.
prs.matters: Tools that set bucket ownership as part of setup work on servers without login.

prs.title: Network drive uploads fail clearly when the folder does not exist
prs.broken: Creating a folder or file inside a folder that did not exist quietly made all the missing folders, though the network drive standard says this must fail.
prs.changed: These requests now fail with the standard conflict error.
prs.matters: A typo in a path shows up as an error instead of leaving stray folders behind.

prs.title: Changing a file's sharing setting works when login is turned off
prs.broken: With login turned off, every attempt to change who can read a file was refused, even right after the same person uploaded it.
prs.changed: With login off, these changes are now allowed, the same way other ownership checks already treat it.
prs.matters: Small setups without accounts can share files without turning on login just for this.

prs.title: File transfer reports a failed delete instead of claiming success
prs.broken: Through the file transfer server, deleting something that was not there, or making a folder that already existed, quietly reported success.
prs.changed: These now fail with the same errors a standard file transfer server gives.
prs.matters: Scripts and people learn when an action did nothing, instead of trusting a false success.

prs.title: Moving a file over another through WebDAV now replaces it
prs.broken: WebDAV clients that move a file onto an existing name often leave out the overwrite setting, which by the standard means yes. The server treated it as no and refused the move.
prs.changed: A move with no overwrite setting now replaces the existing file, as the standard says. An explicit no still refuses.
prs.matters: Saving and renaming files from WebDAV apps works the way people expect.
